what_its_for: Orphenadrine is a muscle relaxer used to relieve pain and stiffness caused by muscle injuries, sprains, or strains. It works by blocking certain signals in your brain and nervous system to help your muscles relax.
how_to_take: Take orphenadrine exactly as your doctor tells you. You can take it with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush, chew, or break it. Drink a full glass of water with each dose. Try to take it at the same times every day to help you remember.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 100 mg (one extended-release tablet) taken twice a day — once in the morning and once in the evening, about 12 hours apart. Do not take more than your doctor prescribes. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on how you respond to the medication.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next scheduled dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never double up or take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store orphenadrine at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medication in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking orphenadrine — it can cause dangerous drowsiness and dizziness. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do anything that requires you to be alert until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid taking other sedatives, sleeping pills, anxiety medications, or opioid pain relievers unless your doctor approves, as these can increase the risk of serious side effects. Tell your doctor about all medications, vitamins, and supplements you are taking.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: fast or pounding heartbeat, difficulty urinating or inability to urinate, severe confusion or hallucinations, blurred vision or eye pain, rash or allergic reaction (hives, swelling, trouble breathing), fainting or feeling lightheaded, or any worsening of your symptoms. Seek emergency help immediately if you think you have taken too much orphenadrine.
when_it_works: Orphenadrine usually begins to work within 1 hour of taking a dose. You may start to notice some relief from muscle pain and stiffness fairly quickly, but it may take a few days of regular use to feel the full benefit. This medication is usually used for short periods of time along with rest and physical therapy.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over) should use orphenadrine with extra caution because they are more sensitive to its side effects, including confusion, dizziness, and difficulty urinating, which can increase the risk of falls. Orphenadrine is generally NOT recommended for use during pregnancy or breastfeeding unless your doctor decides the benefit clearly outweighs the risk — always discuss this with your doctor. This medication is not approved for use in children. Tell your doctor if you have glaucoma, an enlarged prostate, heart problems, kidney disease, or liver disease, as orphenadrine may not be safe for you.
